big_story.headline: Jio Prepares India's Biggest IPO
big_story.subhead: AMBANI SETS ₹30,213 CRORE ISSUE AS JIO PLATFORMS TARGETS ₹10.3 LAKH CRORE VALUATION
paragraphs: Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms has set its price band for what is poised to become India's largest IPO yet. Meta- and Google-backed Jio is aiming to raise up to $3.2 billion through a ₹30,213 crore issue. The share price is set at ₹1,119, giving the digital and telecom powerhouse a massive valuation of ₹10.3 lakh crore as it pitches its long-term growth story to investors.

The upcoming market debut marks a pivotal milestone for parent conglomerate Reliance Industries, with analysts predicting a strong listing pop for the telecom giant. Following the successful listing of Jio Platforms, Reliance Industries could potentially topple Tata to become India's most valuable corporate group. Market observers note that the fresh capital raised will significantly reshape the competitive telecom landscape.

As Jio Platforms prepares for its historic market entry, both domestic and global market participants are closely tracking institutional subscription demand. The record-setting issue serves as a benchmark test for Indian equity market depth and investor appetite for mega-scale technology assets. Success here could trigger a fresh wave of public listings across the country's broader technology ecosystem.
big_story.pullbox: Jio Platforms' ₹30,213 crore issue targets a ₹10.3 lakh crore valuation, marking India's largest IPO to date.

explains.title: What is an Initial Public Offering?
paragraphs: An Initial Public Offering, or IPO, is the process through which a private company sells its shares to the public for the first time. This mechanism allows growing businesses to raise fresh equity capital from both institutional funds and retail investors.

Once an IPO is complete, the company's stock is listed on formal exchanges for public trading. Listing enhances financial transparency, creates liquidity for early venture backers, and subjects the enterprise to regular public reporting standards.

Lunar robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in pre-seed funding to build out its space technology solutions. The round was led by premier venture capital firms Accel and Prosus Ventures, marking an early vote of confidence in India's frontier technology sector.

The newly secured capital will enable Cosmochute to accelerate development of its autonomous lunar robotics platforms and expand core engineering teams. Backing from global funds like Accel and Prosus underscores growing investor interest in commercial space technologies originating out of India.

story_1.headline: RBI Tightens Rules to Curb Rupee Speculation
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has stepped up its defense of the domestic currency by introducing stricter regulations aimed at curbing speculative trading. These fresh measures arrive as ongoing depreciation pressures continue to weigh heavily on foreign exchange markets.

Bankers and traders are closely evaluating how these tighter compliance norms will impact liquidity and hedging strategies in the near term. The central bank remains vigilant as currency volatility persists across emerging markets.

story_2.headline: RBI Clarifies Forex Curbs After Market Swings
paragraphs: Following noticeable swings in currency trading, the Reserve Bank of India has issued clarifications regarding the scope of its recent forex curbs. Market participants had sought regulatory certainty on hedging requirements.
The central bank aims to balance orderly market conditions with necessary flexibility for corporate hedgers as global currency dynamics continue to shift.

story_3.headline: Daily CRR Maintenance Raised to 99%
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India has raised the daily Cash Reserve Ratio maintenance requirement for commercial banks to 99 percent. This regulatory adjustment aims to tighten short-term liquidity management across the banking system.

geopolitics.headline: India-US Trade Deal Nears Finalisation
paragraphs: India and the United States are nearing the finalisation of their bilateral trade pact, with US envoy Sergio Gor stating that big items are done and both sides are close to a landing point. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that the first phase of the trade deal has been finalised and legal drafting is currently under way, keeping changed circumstances in mind. This critical economic milestone moves forward alongside India's broader trade strategy, including the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement coming into force on October 20 and a targeted Canada deal by year-end.

While the legal drafting process proceeds for the US pact, officials must navigate the remaining finer points before the agreement is formally signed and enacted. For Indian businesses and exporters, the successful conclusion of these major international trade deals promises to reshape market access and reduce cross-border frictions. As the first phase is locked in, market participants will watch closely to see how the implementation timeline impacts bilateral commerce and trade deficits.
